territorial_scope.description: Applies within Oregon. Enterprise zones are designated by Oregon cities, counties and ports; reservation zones are limited to named eligible Indian tribes listed in ORS 285C.306(1).

evidence.quote: Any city, county or port may designate an area within the city, county or port as an enterprise zone.

summary.short: Oregon statute (ORS Chapter 285C, 2023 Edition) setting up enterprise zones and tax-incentive programs. Authorized firms can receive property tax exemptions conditioned on employment, wage and investment requirements, administered by the Oregon Business Development Department, zone sponsors and county assessors. Not AI-specific.
summary.long: ORS Chapter 285C (2023 Edition; this part covers ORS 285C.045 to 285C.547 in part, with the remainder in part 2) provides for enterprise zones designated by cities, counties and ports, with designation made final by a positive determination of the Oregon Business Development Department. Eligible business firms that are authorized may receive a 100 percent property tax exemption on qualified property for three tax years, extendable by up to two years by agreement. Exemption depends on employment levels, minimum compensation, first-source hiring agreements and a school support fee, and non-compliance can lead to disqualification and additional taxes. Reservation enterprise zones are available to listed tribes. Rural renewable energy development zones and long-term rural enterprise zone certifications provide property tax exemptions for 7 to 15 years. The chapter also covers a business development income tax exemption through preliminary and annual certification and renewable energy equipment manufacturing tax credits with annual cost limits. Under ORS 285C.255, no area may be designated as an enterprise zone, and no authorization may be obtained under ORS 285C.140, after June 30, 2032. The table of contents also lists a Strategic Investment Program and a Low Income Community Jobs Initiative, whose text is not in this part. The instrument contains no AI-specific provisions.

notes: Part 1 of 2: covers the front matter, the table of contents and ORS 285C.045 through 285C.547 (partial); the ORS 285C.650 to 285C.659 headings and later sections are in part 2. Front matter says the 2024 regular session amended or repealed sections of this chapter and enacted new sections, citing tables that are not reproduced here; this 2023 Edition text does not show those changes. ORS 285C.255 carries a note that it was enacted but not added to ORS chapter 285C. Renumbering histories appear for 285C.045 (formerly 285C.260), 285C.309 (renumbered 315.506 in 2017), 285C.406 (renumbered 285C.408 in 2023) and 285C.450 to 285C.480 (renumbered into ORS 307). Text inconsistency: ORS 285C.408(2)(b) sets a June 30, 2018 certification date for the corporate excise or income tax credit, while 285C.408(2)(a) sets June 30, 2032 for the property tax exemption; both are recorded as written. Target instruments are not in a supplied registry match, so target_instrument_id is left empty. Thresholds, obligations and enforcement in this part are not coded in this pass, since the requested fields are relations, entities and notes. This part covers ORS 285C.547(2) (end of application provisions) through ORS 285C.659. Relations and entities are drawn from this part only. ORS 285C.639 is marked repealed by 2015 c.757 §4. The Preface note says ORS 285C.650, 285C.653, 285C.656 and 285C.659 were enacted but not added to ORS chapter 285C, so their placement in the chapter should be checked against the official compilation. Cross-references to ORS 285C.540 to 285C.559 and ORS 285C.050 are internal to this chapter and are not recorded as relations. Dates and amounts in this part are noted in other sections of the annotation and were not coded here.
